description: Decisions framed as 'Action as proposed' (single-proposal, no A/B/C) still require --selected. The current path is --selected=__other__ --freeform="accept as proposed", which is both awkward and semantically weird — __other__ implies 'none of the above' but the intent is 'yes, the proposed one'. Options: (A) CLI accepts --selected=proposed as sugar that sends the right API payload; (B) API normalizes single-proposal decisions to not require --selected at all; (C) decision-add for single-proposal decisions auto-populates a default option so --selected has a valid key. Prefer B (API-side fix) to avoid papering over the ergonomics at the CLI layer. Surfaced 2026-04-24 walk while accepting 3 of 4 meta-opt decisions, all of which had no A/B/C options.
name: prompt-manager-decision-accept-no-options-ergonomics
title: decision-accept for option-less decisions: allow --selected=proposed sugar or normalize API-side
